skills.name: Standard categorical forms: A, E, I and O

note.text: A, E, I and O name the combinations of quantity and quality. Not all S are P translates as Some S are not P. Universal claims are refuted by appropriate counterexamples; a form label does not establish truth.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to classify and construct the standard forms and identify a counterexample to a universal claim. Builds on: quantity and quality as separate properties. Leads to: distribution and Venn diagrams, which depend on the exact form.

sections.heading: Combine the properties
sections.text: A: All S are P, universal affirmative. E: No S are P, universal negative. I: Some S are P, particular affirmative. O: Some S are not P, particular negative. The letters abbreviate these structures; they do not rank the quality of a pupil’s work or establish truth. Keep the same S and P when comparing forms.

sections.heading: Use the form, not a memorised topic
sections.text: For an invented library, All library books are loanable items is A. No library books are loanable items is E. Some library books are loanable items is I. Some library books are not loanable items is O. The topic is unchanged while quantity and quality vary. A negative form need not contain the separate word not: No signals E.

sections.heading: Check what would refute a claim
sections.text: An S outside P refutes All S are P. An object in both classes refutes No S are P. Not all S are P therefore has O meaning, not E meaning: it leaves open whether other S belong to P. Particular claims need an existing example. Universal-to-particular inferences require an explicit existence assumption under the modern interpretation.

mistake.wrong: Not all members are readers means no members are readers.
mistake.right: It means some members are not readers.
mistake.why: A counterexample to all need not exclude every possible reader.

worked_example.problem: Classify Not all library books are loanable items.
steps: Denying all requires at least one library book outside the loanable class.
Rewrite: Some library books are not loanable items.
This has particular quantity and negative quality.

questions.prompt: An invented club has {inside} members with badges and {outside} without badges. How many counterexamples to All club members are badge holders are shown?

misconceptions.explain: These members satisfy the claim instead of refuting it.
Not every member is a counterexample; count only those without badges.

solution: A counterexample must be a club member outside the badge-holder class.
There are {outside} such members, so the answer is {answer}.
